transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 16:00 EDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Benton (NorthStar CTO), Ben Morales (Infra), Priya Rao (Compliance), Evan Kim (ML Platform)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on requirements for a fully air-gapped, on-prem deployment for NorthStar's clinical NLP and summarization pipelines. Discussed offline updates, patching cadence, hardware constraints (PCIe lanes, power, NVMe space), KMS/HSM considerations, and pilot scope. Agreed to exchange docs and set on-site ops session.

Topics: Air-gapped update process; hardware sizing (A100 vs H100 vs 4090 clusters); KV cache persistence strategies; offline patch signing; network isolation; compliance evidence; timeline for pilot; fallback to dedicated during maintenance windows.

[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Dr. Laura Benton (NorthStar): Laura here.
[00:08] Ben Morales (Infra): Ben on infra.
[00:10] Priya Rao (Compliance): Priya here.
[00:12] Evan Kim (ML Platform): Evan.
[00:15] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus here, hi. Nina on the line too.
[00:18] Nina Patel (Redwood SE): Hey all.

[00:25] Sophie: Goal for today is to understand what NorthStar needs for an offline private deployment — air-gapped legal/regulatory constraints, how you want updates delivered, and what success looks like for a pilot.
[00:35] Dr. Laura Benton: Yup. We're regulated healthcare, PHI in some flows, and compliance wants a fully air-gapped option for any model that sees PHI or PII. We also have a requirement that updates cannot be pulled from the internet. Everything has to be pushed in via an approved bundle.
[00:48] Priya: And audit trails — we need signed artifacts and proof of integrity, and key management that meets our KMS/HSM policy.
[00:55] Marcus: Got it. We support both a private on-prem package and instructions for air-gapped installs. For updates we typically prepare an 'offline update bundle' — it's a signed tarball containing the runtime, model artifacts, and migration scripts. That tarball can be verified with your HSM public key. In practice it's like a sneaker-net deploy or via secure jump host.
[01:14] Ben: Sneaker-net, yep that's our favorite term. A few Qs up front: our racks are power-constrained in one DC (max 40A per PDU), and most of our current infra is dual-socket CPU hosts with 2x 80GB GPUs. We also have a few B4 instances — sorry, bad brain, Nvidia 4080-ish workstations — for dev. How sensitive is the runtime to NVMe and PCIe topology?
[01:36] Marcus: Good question. The runtime is sensitive when you do large KV cache persistence and model swap. For ideal latency/throughput, NVMe local for model shards and fast PCIe for GPUs is preferred. If you are trying to squeeze into 2x 80GB GPUs per host, we recommend capturing the sequence length and concurrency in your workload — we'll size the batch/worker config accordingly. If you only have a single NVMe per host or shared storage, we can change the model streaming strategy to reduce I/O but that will add latency.
[02:00] Evan: We're evaluating two main workloads: real-time clinical note summarization (low latency target: p95 < 250ms for short prompts) and bulk de-identification jobs (throughput-biased). Can Redwood do a split: low-latency model pinned to dedicated GPUs and batch pipeline on cheaper quantized variants?
[02:19] Nina: Absolutely. Typical pattern is hot path on dedicated capacity (we call it Dedicated or Private pinned), and batch on quantized replicas. We can recommend quantization profiles — we've seen 4-bit q4 or 8-bit for de-id jobs. There's trade-off on quality, but you get 3-4x throughput improvements.
[02:34] Priya: How do you validate quality regressions? We need eval hooks and regression alerts tied to test prompts.
[02:40] Marcus: We have an Optimize-style eval harness — you can bring your test set and we'll run per-release regression checks. For offline deployments we provide the same harness as an executable that runs inside your environment and outputs signed reports you can include in audits.
[02:52] Priya: Signed reports — good. Who signs them? Is that Redwood's signature?
[02:56] Sophie: Redwood signs the release bundle. For regression reports you can also configure a mutual attestation where your HSM signs the local verification. We can send an architecture note.

[03:05] Ben: Patching cadence — we prefer quarterly maintenance windows, but security wants emergency hotfix process. How do you handle emergency CVEs for the runtime or models?
[03:14] Marcus: There are two tracks: normal scheduled releases (we'll ship quarterly or when you ask), and security hotfixes. For an air-gapped environment, hotfixes come as a signed delta bundle. You can choose to accept and apply immediately or route through your change control. We can also produce a pre-signed, time-limited patch if you need immediate mitigations.
[03:34] Dr. Laura: And what about software attestations — SBOMs, binary hashes, provenance?
[03:39] Nina: We'll provide SBOM, binary hashes, signed release manifests, and a mapping of which kernel optimizations are enabled. Some customers also require reproducible builds; we can supply build artifacts and instructions to reproduce on-prem.

[03:52] Evan: On key management, we can't have private keys leave our HSM. Does Redwood support integrating with customer HSM for model decryption at rest?
[03:59] Marcus: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For model encryption at rest the decryption keys stay in your HSM. Our agent calls the local KMS endpoint. For attestation, the update bundle is encrypted with your public key and signed by Redwood's release key.
[04:15] Ben: Any assumptions about outbound network access during install? Our process forbids outbound to unknown endpoints but we can allow a jump host with restricted egress to a named IP during staging.
[04:26] Sophie: The offline install does not require outbound from the cluster. You can use a controlled jumphost to transfer the bundle. We only need connectivity for future telemetry if you opt-in; telemetry is fully configurable and can be disabled.

[04:38] Dr. Laura: Telemetry — we need guarantee that logs containing PHI never leave the air-gapped environment.
[04:44] Nina: By default all telemetry is scrubbed and aggregated; for air-gapped deployments we disable telemetry by default and ship a telemetry export tool you can run internally to create anonymized metrics snapshots.

[04:56] [05:00] Sophie: Let's talk models and quantization: do you plan to run open models or is there a plan to bring a private fine-tuned model?
[05:08] Evan: We'll likely fine-tune an open model internally and then want to host a fine-tuned checkpoint. Size TBD — the candidate is a 30B family. Curious about optimal format, shards, and whether we should convert to a fused-quantized artifact.
[05:24] Marcus: For 30B models we often recommend sharding across NVMe and using fused 4-bit quant for batch jobs; for low-latency hot path we can keep a mixed precision float path if you have H100s. If you're limited to consumer 4080/4090s we can still run quantized runtimes but memory and kernel support differs — we can share a compatibility matrix.
[05:45] Ben: Compatibility matrix would be very helpful — include driver versions, CUDA, cuDNN, and required kernel patch levels. Some of our hosts are on older kernels and we have strict change windows.
[05:57] Marcus: We'll include that. Also note that for air-gapped installs we bundle the exact driver binaries and container images, so you don't need to fetch from public registries.

[06:08] Priya: Audit logging — we need immutable logs showing who requested what, model version, prompt hash, and whether output was stored. We also need tamper-evidence.
[06:18] Nina: We support append-only audit logs with HMAC chains and optional push into your SIEM via an offline export. For tamper evidence, we can timestamp entries and sign log bundles with your HSM.
[06:30] [06:35] Evan: On fallback: if a node goes down or you need maintenance, can we fail-over to a hosted Redwood Dedicated region temporarily? We might want a hybrid mode during upgrades.
[06:44] Sophie: Yes — hybrid fallback is supported, but you must accept network egress for requests routed out. For PHI flows you'd need to ensure agreement on data residency and maybe anonymization before routing out. Some customers opt to route only non-PHI tasks to hosted.

[06:58] Dr. Laura: Our legal team would be hesitant. We'll likely keep PHI traffic strictly on-prem and route synthetic or non-PHI workloads for external fallback.
[07:07] Sophie: Totally understandable. We'll document the gating and consent flows.

[07:15] Ben: Curious about KV cache persistence — does Redwood expect an in-memory only cache or do you persist KV to disk for restart recovery?
[07:23] Marcus: We support both. For p95 latency we often keep KV in memory and warm with checkpointing to NVMe; for long-running multi-turn chat state we persist periodic snapshots so restart is faster. In air-gapped setups we can tune snapshot frequency, retention, and how snapshots are signed and verified.
[07:40] Evan: Any specific filesystem recommendations? XFS, ext4, ZFS?
[07:44] Marcus: XFS with DAX is common for speed; ZFS for replication-inclined shops. We'll include our tested profiles.

[07:52] Priya: Who will own SOC2 evidence? We need both Redwood's SOC2 plus a map of controls that apply in private deployment and what NorthStar still owns.
[08:01] Sophie: We'll share a control mapping and a SOC2 summary. For private deployments the control boundary shifts — e.g., Redwood owns the software build and release controls; NorthStar owns physical host security, key management, and certain patching processes. We'll produce a shared RACI.

[08:16] [08:20] Dr. Laura: Timeline — ideally pilot inside 6-8 weeks, with on-site workshop and a 4-week validation window. Is that realistic?
[08:27] Marcus: It's tight but doable if we get hardware inventory and an ops contact. Workshop in week 2, image prep week 3, pilot deploy week 4, validation weeks 5-8. The gating items are hardware compatibility, change window approvals, and signed NDA for any model checkpoint transfers.
[08:42] Priya: NDA and data processing addendum we'll need before any PHI model checkpoint leaves our network.

[08:49] Sophie: We'll circulate legal templates and the DPA.

[08:55] Evan: A few edge-case questions: 1) Can we run inside VMs or require bare metal? 2) GPU sharing for multi-tenant? 3) Do you support MIG on A100/H100?
[09:05] Marcus: 1) We support VM-based deployments but bare metal gives better determinism. 2) We don't recommend GPU sharing for production low-latency use — it complicates tail latency. For batch you can multiplex. 3) We support MIG for certain workloads — we can provide recommended configurations and caveats.

[09:20] Ben: Power and heat — recommend rack level planning guidance?
[09:23] Marcus: We'll provide thermal and power profiles per GPU model and per cluster size. Also placement suggestions to avoid over-subscribing PDUs.

[09:33] [09:40] Priya: Can we get a sample offline update bundle to vet? We want to validate signature verification and the install script.
[09:47] Nina: Yes — we'll provide a redteam-style sample bundle (non-prod) and step-by-step install doc. It includes a verification script that checks signatures against a provided public key.

[09:58] Evan: What about model licensing and redistribution? If we ship an open model but fine-tune it, what constraints are there?
[10:04] Sophie: Licensing depends on the base model. We'll help map license obligations and include them in the bundle metadata. For fine-tuned artifacts you control distribution, but we can advise best practices in the DPA.

[10:13] Ben: Any special requirement for the container runtime? We use podman and some of our infra is OCI-based but air-gap may prefer containerd.
[10:20] Marcus: We support Docker, containerd, and podman. For air-gapped we supply signed container images and OCI archives.

[10:29] Dr. Laura: Ok let's recap and call out blockers.
[10:33] Sophie: Recap — Redwood will: 1) Send air-gap deployment checklist and a sample offline bundle; 2) Share compatibility matrix and driver/container versions; 3) Provide SOC2 control mapping and DPA templates; 4) Draft GPU sizing guidance and quantization recommendations. NorthStar will: 1) Share hardware inventory and rack PDU details; 2) Confirm internal change windows and jump host availability; 3) Legal to review NDA/DPA.

[10:57] Priya: Action item: Compliance will review the sample bundle and sign-off process, aim to provide feedback by next week.
[11:04] Sophie: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[11:07] Ben: One last thing — can you list the minimum NVMe per model shard?
[11:10] Marcus: We'll put that in the compatibility doc with numbers by model size.

[11:15] Dr. Laura: Thank you everyone.
[11:17] Sophie: Thanks, we’ll follow up with the docs.

End of transcript.
